onb.feature.name: First-year tutorial
onb.feature.desc: A mentor guides you through the first year via in-game mail.
onb.param.pause.tip: The game pauses when the mail of a new tutorial step arrives.
onb.param.reminders.tip: The mentor reminds you if you stay on one step for long.
onb.toggle.label: Tutorial
onb.toggle.tooltip: A mentor guides you through the first year via in-game mail.
onb.start.notify: Mentor: the first mail arrives as soon as time runs — press ▶.
onb.notify.title: Mentor's hint
onb.button.skipStep.tip: Mark the step as skipped and move on to the next one.
onb.button.skipAll.tip: End the tutorial. Mails that have already arrived stay in the inbox.
onb.button.hint.tip: Show the next hint for this step.
onb.hint.none: No more hints for this step
onb.hub.title: Tutorial
onb.hub.restart.title: Restart the tutorial?
onb.hub.restart.body: The step statuses of this game will be reset. Steps you have already done are counted at once, and the mail comes for the first step not done yet.
onb.error.content: Tutorial content is broken: see Player.log
onb.welcome.title: [Mentor] Welcome to {0}
onb.welcome.name: Welcome
onb.welcome.body: {1}, I'll guide you through your first year. Each mail is one action. I'll notice when you do it and send the next one; there is nothing to confirm. You can pause time with the button at the bottom of the screen — I'll wait. If you already know the game, press "Skip tutorial" below; you can also do it later from the Mods menu. What to do now: nothing. Read this mail — the next one arrives tomorrow.
onb.research.title: [Mentor] First research
onb.research.name: First research
onb.research.body: Science first. Research unlocks new technologies: process nodes, packages, memory, frequencies. Without it you can only build what the starting set allows. Open the Research window on the desktop, pick a technology in the tree and start it. One research runs at a time; it costs money and takes game days. Research speed grows with funding, but slowly: twice the money gives about 1.4 times the daily progress. Don't drain your cash to speed it up. What to do now: open the Research window and start any research.
onb.research.hint1: No research chosen yet. Open Research on the desktop and click a technology in the tree, for example a process node or a package.
onb.research.hint2: Without research there will be no new parts, and your rivals don't stand still. Pick a technology that will improve your CPU and start it.
onb.design_cpu.title: [Mentor] Your first CPU
onb.design_cpu.name: CPU project
onb.design_cpu.body: Now the product. In the Create Hardware window open "New CPU" and put a project together: package, memory, process node, number of cores, die size, frequency, cache. The game recalculates the specs with every slider you move, so watch performance, power consumption and temperature. A CPU that is too hot or too hungry sells worse. For your first one, don't chase records: pick a sensible middle option and look at the cost and time of the project. Development takes time and costs money every day. What to do now: press "Open CPU designer", build a CPU and start the project.
onb.design_cpu.body.fabless: Now the product. In the Create Hardware window open "New CPU" and put a project together: package, memory, process node, number of cores, die size, frequency, cache. You have no factory of your own, so pick a process node licensed from a foundry: the foundry will produce your CPU. The game recalculates the specs with every slider you move, so watch performance, power consumption and temperature. For a first CPU don't chase records: development takes time and costs money every day. What to do now: press "Open CPU designer", build a CPU and start the project.
onb.design_cpu.hint1: The CPU project isn't started yet. Open Create Hardware > New CPU, choose the parts and press "Create".
onb.design_cpu.hint2: For a first CPU the simplest set will do: any available package, memory and process node, and the fewest cores. What matters is to start the project; you can improve later.
onb.dev_wait.title: [Mentor] Development is under way
onb.dev_wait.name: CPU development
onb.dev_wait.body: The project is running: its card with the progress has appeared in the side panel. While a CPU is in development, money leaves your account every day. You can speed time up with the speed buttons at the bottom of the screen. Don't rush blindly: watch the money in the corner of the screen so it doesn't go negative. When the project ends, the game opens the CPU release window by itself. That is where the price is set — the next mail covers it. What to do now: nothing. Let time run and wait for the project to finish.
onb.release_price.title: [Mentor] Pricing your CPU
onb.release_price.name: Price and release
onb.release_price.body: When development ends, the release window opens, and the price is set there. It is the most important decision for sales. Buyers are split into segments, each with its own budget: High End {0}, Mid Range {1}, Low End {2}, Industries {3}. A price above the budget drops the CPU's rating, and at three budgets or more the segment won't buy it at all. A price below the budget raises the rating instead. A new CPU starts at 0.05 popularity out of 1.0 in every segment, and it grows mostly from sales. So for the first CPU choose a price near the budget of your segment, not a record one. What to do now: when the release window opens, set the price by the budget of your segment and release the CPU.
onb.production.title: [Mentor] Starting production
onb.production.name: Starting production
onb.production.body: A released CPU doesn't sell by itself: it has to be produced. With no production the warehouse is empty and sales hit "out of stock". In the Production window every CPU has a lines slider. More lines mean more units a day, but your factory has exactly as many lines as were built, and you split them among all your CPUs. Finished CPUs sit in the warehouse, and storage costs $0.5 per unit per month, so don't pile them up. If demand is higher than output, the game shows missed sales. What to do now: open the Production window and assign lines to your new CPU.
onb.production.body.fabless: A released CPU doesn't sell by itself: it has to be produced. You have no factory of your own, so a foundry makes it, the one whose process node you picked while designing. Lines are assigned automatically: such a CPU has no slider. Look into the Production window and check that your CPU is there and its output is running. The foundry charges a markup for production, and it is already included in the unit cost. Finished CPUs sit in the warehouse, and storage costs $0.5 per unit per month. What to do now: open the Production window and check that your CPU's output has started.
onb.production.hint1: Production hasn't started. Open the Production window: the CPU must have lines assigned (for a fabless company the foundry assigns them).
onb.production.hint2: The warehouse is still empty. In the Production window check that the CPU has lines assigned and that other CPUs or contracts haven't taken them.
onb.first_sales.title: [Mentor] First sales
onb.first_sales.name: First sales
onb.first_sales.body: The CPU is in stock: time to sell. Sales happen by themselves every day: buyers pick the best CPU by rating, price and popularity. The first days can pass with no sales. That's normal: a new CPU has 0.05 popularity out of 1.0, and it grows with purchases. But if there are no sales for weeks, the price is almost always to blame. Keep an eye on the CPU card in the side panel and on the Market window: they show how much was sold, how much is left in stock and what your market share is. What to do now: wait for the first sales; if there are none, compare the price with the budget of the segment.
onb.first_sales.hint1: No sales? A price above the segment's budget (Low End: {0}) cuts the rating, and at three budgets the segment won't buy at all. Compare the price with the budget and check the stock in the Production window.
onb.first_sales.hint2: Still no sales. Check three things: the price is not above the segment's budget, there are CPUs in stock, and the CPU's performance and power consumption are fine for its time. Lower the price and wait a few days.
onb.oem_offer.title: [Mentor] Contracts with manufacturers
onb.oem_offer.name: Manufacturer contract
onb.oem_offer.body: Orders have appeared in the Contracts window: computer and console makers are looking for a CPU and pay for every unit. It is steady demand on top of the market. An order states the performance it needs, the power consumption it allows, how many units a month and how much it pays per unit. Pick an order your CPU fits and send an offer. The client decides a year after the order appears and chooses among the offers itself. Mind the obligations: the penalty for undersupply is twice the payment per unit. Don't offer more than your production can carry. What to do now: open Contracts and send an offer. Or switch on "Automatically sign contracts": then on December 31 the offers go out by themselves at the profit margin you set (40% by default).
onb.oem_offer.hint1: Orders are sitting idle. In the Contracts window open a suitable order and send an offer with your CPU, or switch on "Automatically sign contracts".
onb.oem_offer.hint2: Not every CPU fits every order: it needs enough performance and power consumption below the limit of the order. If none of your CPUs fits, that's fine: come back to the orders after your next release.
onb.finance.title: [Mentor] Company finances
onb.finance.name: Finances
onb.finance.body: A new month has started, a good moment to look at the money. You have {0} in the account. The details are in the Finance window: income, expenses and profit by month. Two things eat money quietly: profit tax is 25% of the monthly profit, and interest on debt is 25% a year. Tax is paid on profit only, while a debt keeps growing until you repay it. If you run short, the bank will lend, but the limit is finite, and beyond it a default begins. Better to keep a reserve for a few months of expenses. What to do now: open the Finance window and see which expense is the biggest.
onb.graduation.title: [Mentor] Tutorial complete
onb.graduation.name: Tutorial summary
onb.graduation.body: You have finished the tutorial. The summary by step is at the end of this mail. From here you are on your own. Watch the money and don't borrow without a plan, keep an eye on stock and price, and release new CPUs before the old ones age: the popularity of an old CPU falls. This is my last mail. You can start the tutorial again from the Mods menu. What to do now: keep playing.
onb.foundry_services.title: [Mentor] Foundry services
onb.foundry_services.name: Foundry services
onb.foundry_services.body: You are a foundry: you don't design CPUs, you produce them for other companies. Your clients are fabless companies that have no factory. For them to order from you, switch on "Foundry Services" in the Production window. While it is off, clients can't see you. Clients need free lines and modern process nodes, so keep both in mind when you plan the factory. What to do now: open the Production window and make sure "Foundry Services" is on.
onb.foundry_services.hint1: Services are still off. In the Production window find the "Foundry Services" switch and turn it on: without it there will be no orders.
onb.first_client.title: [Mentor] Your first client
onb.first_client.name: First client
onb.first_client.body: Now you need a client. Fabless companies offer you production contracts: they appear in the Contracts window, in the Business section. A contract is an agreement to produce their CPUs on your lines. A contract states the markup the client pays, 5% royalties and when it ends. It occupies part of your lines, so don't sign more than you can produce: failing to deliver means penalties. Start with one small contract and see how your lines fill up. What to do now: open Contracts and press "Sign Contract" on your first production contract.
onb.first_client.hint1: No client yet. Open Contracts, the Business section, and look at the offered contracts: pick one that fits your free lines and sign it.
onb.first_client.hint2: Clients choose foundries with free lines and a modern process node. If nobody is interested, check how many lines are free and think about expanding the factory.
onb.factory_expansion.title: [Mentor] Expanding the factory
onb.factory_expansion.name: Factory expansion
onb.factory_expansion.body: The more lines you have, the more contracts you can carry. When all your lines are taken by clients, you can't accept a new order, so expand the factory ahead of time. An expansion is a project: it costs money and takes time, like developing a CPU. The new lines appear only when the project is done. After an expansion the running cost of the factory grows too, so expand for real demand, not just in case. What to do now: press "Open factory expansion" and start an expansion project.
onb.factory_expansion.hint1: Running out of lines? Open "Factory expansion", pick how many lines to add and start the project: it costs money and takes time, so begin early.
onb.tip_debt.title: [Mentor] You owe the bank
onb.tip_debt.body: You have gone into the red. The bank lends up to {0} at 25% a year; interest accrues until the debt is repaid. Below that limit a default begins: you get {1} days to fix it, then bankruptcy. A default isn't the end, but it is a very expensive mistake. There is one way out: bring the balance back above zero. Stop unnecessary spending, sell off the stock, cut the price of a CPU that sits in the warehouse. And remember the profit tax, 25%. What to do now: open the Finance window, find the biggest expenses and cut them.
onb.tip_default.title: [Mentor] You are in default
onb.tip_default.body: You are in default: the debt has passed the bank's limit. You have {0} days until bankruptcy; after that the company closes and the game is over. While those days last, everything can still be fixed: bring the debt back within the bank's limit and the default ends. Money is needed urgently: sell off the stock, stop spending, drop whatever earns nothing. Don't wait for the last day: interest on the debt, 25% a year, grows every day. What to do now: cut expenses and raise revenue before the time runs out.
onb.tip_default.body.rec: You are in default: {0} days until bankruptcy. Open the Rescue menu: it offers ways to save the company (sell production lines, sell off the stock, retire a CPU, go fabless) and shows the price of every step. Don't wait: interest on the debt, 25% a year, grows every day. What to do now: open the Rescue menu and pick an option.
onb.tip_contract_signed.title: [Mentor] Contract signed
onb.tip_contract_signed.body: The contract is signed, and now you have to fulfil it. The client expects the agreed number of CPUs every month, and part of your lines is taken by the contract. The penalty for undersupply is twice the payment for every missing unit, so a missed delivery hurts the cash more than lost profit. Make sure the lines and the stock are enough for both the contract and the market, and don't take on new obligations until you are sure you cope. What to do now: open the Production window and check that you have enough lines for the contract.
onb.tip_missed_sales.title: [Mentor] You are losing sales
onb.tip_missed_sales.body: For a week now there have been more missed sales than sales made: buyers want your CPU, but there isn't enough of it in stock. The cause is almost always the same: not enough production. Assign more lines to the CPU in the Production window. If there are no free lines, expand the factory: it is a project that costs money and takes time. While lines are short, don't cut the price: demand is already higher than output. What to do now: press "Open factory expansion" or assign more lines to the CPU.
onb.tip_year_summary.title: [Mentor] Year in review
onb.tip_year_summary.body: A new year has started, and the game has sent the "Year Summary" mail. You have {0} in the account. The report shows revenue, expenses, taxes and profit for the year. Compare it with the previous one: is revenue growing and does the profit margin hold. If profit is falling, look for the cause: price, stock, an old CPU or development that costs too much. What to do now: read the Year Summary in your inbox and decide what to improve this year.
onb.tip_old_cpu.title: [Mentor] A CPU is getting old
onb.tip_old_cpu.body: One of your CPUs is old: the game counts a CPU as old after 7 years (after 5 years from 1990). The popularity of an old CPU falls every day, and it has fewer and fewer buyers. That is the normal course of things. To keep your sales, release a new generation: design a CPU on more modern parts. You can retire the old one: it leaves the market together with its contracts, and the stock in the warehouse is sold off. Decide when it has stopped earning. What to do now: open Create Hardware and start a project for a new CPU.
